transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have an opportunity to run Furnace 4 overnight for a heat-treated brackets production run. Before I authorize this unusual shift, I need to hear from Workforce Planning and Environmental Health and Safety. Please report any relevant staffing, training, permit, or atmospheric-control requirements we need to address. Let's start with Workforce Planning — what do we need to know about staffing and qualified operators for this overnight run?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I checked the training records this afternoon. Exactly three operators are certified for Furnace 4, and all three must be assigned to the overnight run to cover loading, controls, and unloading. The overnight shift is scheduled as an exact 10-hour shift. I should also note that the workforce roster has not yet synchronized this update to the production schedule.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag an important permit requirement for the overnight Furnace 4 run. I completed a permit review today after this week's argon-cylinder replacement, and it requires continuous oxygen monitoring during the overnight run with the alarm set at exactly 19.5% oxygen, plus a documented purge verification before loading. The authorization for this run must include a purge-verification commitment. I should also note that I have not yet updated the furnace permit packet with these requirements, so we need to account for that before proceeding.
